key_insight: The paper argues that formal theorem proving can be improved beyond standard auto-regressive generation by using a diffusion-based approach. This shifts proof generation from token-by-token prediction to a more global, iterative refinement process that better handles long proofs.
problem_solved: It addresses the limitations of auto-regressive LLMs in formal theorem proving, especially long-range coherence issues, error accumulation, and difficulty recovering from early mistakes during proof generation.
method: Replace pure next-token generation with a diffusion-style proof synthesis and refinement process.
Iteratively denoise or improve partial proof states to produce more coherent formal outputs.
Target formal theorem proving tasks where global structure matters more than purely local token prediction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new direction for reasoning models that may be more reliable on structured, high-precision tasks like theorem proving. It could also inspire broader non-autoregressive or hybrid decoding methods for complex generation problems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline: auto-regressive generation vs diffusion-based proof generation
Error accumulation diagram showing how mistakes propagate in AR models
Iterative refinement loop illustration for proof denoising
Icons representing theorem, logic, and model refinement
paper_title: Diffusion-Proof: Recipe for Formal Theorem Proving Beyond Auto-Regressive Generation
paper_authors: Ruida Wang, Rui Pan, Pengcheng Wang, Shizhe Diao, Tong Zhang
